paper.title_en: Interfacing Silicon Nitride Nanophotonics with Cuprous Oxide Rydberg Excitons
paper.abstract_en: Rydberg excitons in cuprous oxide (Cu$_2$O), the solid-state counterpart of Rydberg atoms, are hydrogen-like electron--hole quasi-particles with micron-sized wavefunctions and strong long-range interactions that promise optical nonlinearities at the few-photon level. Exploiting them in a waveguide quantum electrodynamics (WQED) setting can enable what atomic Rydberg platforms achieve only with ultrahigh vacuum and laser cooling/trapping---a guided optical mode interfaced with the Rydberg medium---while adding the scalability and advanced fabrication of integrated photonics. Here we demonstrate a monolithic, CMOS-compatible interface of Cu$_2$O Rydberg excitons with a SiN$_x$ nanophotonic waveguide. Under non-resonant excitation, excitonic emission from the Cu$_2$O microcrystal is coupled to the guided mode, routed along the waveguide, and collected from an output grating. The spectrum shows the phonon-assisted 1$s$ orthoexciton emission together with the low-lying 2$p$ and 3$p$ lines of the yellow Rydberg series. Spatially selective excitation excludes substrate background and direct scatter, and the enhanced linear polarization of the grating-collected signal identifies the TE-like guided mode as the collection channel. These results establish the complete material--device--measurement stack for a novel platform of nonlinear quantum nanophotonics based on Rydberg excitons.
